body: What's the curl_version()? #6260 changed the way we initialize openssl >= 1.1.0. Try reverting 1835cb9.

Ironic that this is exactly what I was afraid could happen.

@anatol what OpenSSL version is this? The crash is **inside** OpenSSL which makes me maybe lean towards this being a OpenSSL issue rather. Does this program use OpenSSL in other ways as well than via libcurl?

@jay reverting https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/1835cb916e0d40eb8bc1165d5627a0b64f911bac fixes my issue.

@bagder my current openssl version is `1.1.1.h-1`. It is the version that the tool is dynamically linked with. The tool itself (`pulseUi`) is a proprietary binary.
@mattcaswell any idea what we did wrong here

Hmm. Strange. This is happening quite early in libssl initialisation. Libcrypto has been successfully initialised and then libssl fails in its early init steps adding ciphers. Specifically it falls over on this one:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/ad8e83cf11187388c71cfbdb70880d9e7ed26e0e/ssl/ssl_init.c#L62-L63

Does it always crash at exactly this point (same line number in ssl_init.c)? This line doesn't do anything very different to all the other lines that have succeeded immediately before it. The only thing different about this line is that it is enclosed in an `OPENSSL_NO_ARIA` guard.

Is it possible that you have  mismatched libcrypto/libssl versions? If your libcrypto was compiled with `no-aria` but your libssl was not then this could explain that crash.

> If your libcrypto was compiled with no-aria but your libssl was not then this could explain that crash.

I can totally see it possible. pulseUi is a proprietary tool built by https://www.pulsesecure.net/ and they do not share any sources unfortunately. ssl version they use might have different compilation flags.

> I can totally see it possible.

This seems like the most likely explanation to me (at least I can't immediately think of an alternative).

Are there multiple versions of libcrypto/libssl installed on your machine? Possibly there could be library path issues for the user running this application that means the wrong version is being picked up?? Or alternatively you might need to take this up with pulsesecure to get to the bottom of it.

I'm getting this exact same error with curl 7.74.0 on Arch and downgrading to 7.73.0 fixes the issue like @anatol describes. I can provide any extra information and compare it against other environments if necessary.

Any chance a user of the **pulseUI VPN client** could contact them and ask them to join this conversation?

I have reached out, but I have no better "in" than their `info@` email address and I'm worried that won't reach the proper people.

**I urge all users of this "pulseUI VPN client" to report this problem to the provider of the software**. This is the only software we get reports about with this problem - meaning that we are unlikely to revert this change and therefore this is how things will work going forward.

Feel most welcome to point them to this issue. If they can point out any mistakes in our end, that would be awesome too.

If they don't fix their side or respond, I would suggest you consider switching to another VPN client.

I posted into their community support forums to hopefully bring some sort of awareness to this issue:

https://community.pulsesecure.net/t5/Pulse-Desktop-Clients/Linux-Pulse-Client-does-not-work-with-curl-7-74/td-p/44378/jump-to/first-unread-message
